newsitem.title: USA: Vigil for Burmese doctor on Int'l Rights Day.
newsitem.headline: Vigil for Burmese doctor on Int'l Rights Day.

text.p: About 300 people marked International Human Rights Day on Tuesday with an evening vigil against human rights abuses in Burma, and especially the treatment of one doctor.

Ma Thida, 30, a physician and author who served as a campaign aide to Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi, was sentenced to 20 years in prison for distributing leaflets three years ago, officials from Amnesty International and Physician for Human Rights said. She is one of five winners of this year's Reebok Human Rights Award.
Organisers said they hoped the event, in which the rock band R.E.M.'s lead singer Michael Stipe took part, would spotlight the situation in Burma.

The government, the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), seized power in 1988. The U.S.-based human rights group Human Rights Watch/Asia said earlier on Tuesday that scores of Burmese students detained after recent street protests were still being held incommunicado by the military government.
The government said it detained some 860 students in protests over the past week but released all of them shortly afterward.

The "majority of the population in Burma feel helpless, feel hopeless ... but getting this award is a way of putting pressure on the political leaders. It gives people in Burma a feeling of being recognised and being heard," Myiang Myiang Nyunt, who will be accepting the award for Ma Thida, said in an interview.
